questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The language played a big role for me in choosing this location - being able to speak with the locals and receiving proper education was important to me. Furthermore, Scotland is a beautiful country with vast and breathtaking nature, which I wanted to explore. Lastly, Edinburgh is a beautiful city and two of my friends had already gone on exchange there and recommended it.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy even though I had to put some effort into finding the information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a meeting with a representative from the School of Biology - who showed me around campus and guided me through my studies. Moreover, I received informative mails and talked to guides at my accomodation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite difficult since on semester exchange students weren't prioritized. I had to call many times to secure a place.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The place was very worn down. The beds were in bad shape and were very uncomfortable and there isn't any living room.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was quite simple. I received an e-mail, that invited me to create an account for their system. Afterwards, I just chose the courses that I wanted to register for.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Student service and mails that offered guidance.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful. Everything went smoothly.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is possible to get courses that have peculiar requirements - even when you don't live up to the requirements.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses had a level that matched the ones at my home university.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Mostly the same. However, one course had flipped learning where we had to watch the lectures at home online before showing up for recap sessions. This was not great.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Immunology 3, Molecular Genetics 3, and Molecular and Synthetic Plant Biology 3.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Immunology 3 since the lectures, laboratory, and course work was great and the course offered a great entrance knowledge into immunology.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I was suprised about how pricey it was to join different societies.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and drinks were generelly a bit cheaper in the supermarkets - compared to Denmark. However, eating out a restuarants was really expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were so many activities so I am not going to name them all. However, I think there was a society for almost every type of sport, a lot of cultural and food related clubs, and more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the Hillwalking Club and the Squash Club. I had no prior experience in any of them and I thrived. Furtermore, the people are nice and the events are easily comprehensible.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend that they try hiking. It could be Arthurs Seat, the Pentlands or something futher away. I also recommend that they try out the pubs, the student theater (Bedlam), the national museum and gallery, and the hot chocolate.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy - the humor and way of acting was quite similar to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join societies - otherwise it's impossible.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find anything challenging,

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That people always said hello on hikes and that the city was very chill and mellow.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Try to find accomodation outside of the University. Use
sparerooms.co.uk
, Facebook or other platforms. 2. Join a club or a society. You may think that it is a waste of time or to expensive - but it is an excellent way to meet other people. 3. The course requirements are not that serious.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try a real scottish breakfeast!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning about myself and what I wanted to do. Becoming more aware of myself.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To find "true" friends. It was easy to meet people and create relations, but it was hard to make "true" friends because of the short time of the exchange. Therefore, I missed my friends at home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
